blocks.html: The language databases actually speak. Create a database, build a table, drop in some rows, then ask it questions — one interactive slide at a time.
From databases to your first queries — a beginner-friendly guide to structured data.

blocks.text: mysql> SELECT * FROM knowledge;█

blocks.html: SQL (Structured Query Language) is the standard language for talking to relational databases.
The world's most popular open-source database
Used by Facebook, Twitter, YouTube and thousands of other applications worldwide.
SQL is not case-sensitive — SELECT = select = Select. But writing keywords in UPPERCASE is standard practice.
Every column in a table must have a data type — it tells MySQL what kind of value to expect.

blocks.text:
CREATE DATABASE school_db;
USE school_db;

CREATE TABLE students (
  id      INT PRIMARY KEY,
  name    VARCHAR(100),
  age     INT,
  email   VARCHAR(150),
  gpa     DECIMAL(3,2)
);

items: PRIMARY KEY — unique identifier for each row

blocks.text:
INSERT INTO table_name
  (column1, column2, ...)
VALUES
  (value1, value2, ...);

INSERT INTO students (id, name, age, email, gpa)
VALUES
  (1, 'Alice', 20, 'alice@uni.edu', 3.80),
  (2, 'Bob',   22, 'bob@uni.edu',  3.50),
  (3, 'Carol', 21, 'carol@uni.edu',3.90);

blocks.html: INSERT INTO which table to add rows to
VALUES the actual data — match column order!
Result — students table now has rows
💡 You must supply a value for id — it is the PRIMARY KEY and must be unique for every row.

blocks.text:
SELECT name, gpa
FROM students;

blocks.html: ⭐ Use SELECT * for exploration; use specific columns in real apps for speed.
💡 Use LIKE '%term%' to search text — e.g. WHERE name LIKE 'A%' finds all names starting with A.
💡 Add LIMIT 10 at the end to get only the top N results — great for leaderboards!

blocks.text:
-- Bob got a better grade!
UPDATE students
SET gpa = 3.75
WHERE id = 2;

-- Update multiple columns
UPDATE students
SET age = 23, email = 'bob.new@uni.edu'
WHERE id = 2;

blocks.html: ⚠️ Always use WHERE! Without it, every row gets updated — a common mistake!

blocks.text:
DELETE FROM table
WHERE condition;

blocks.html: DELETE FROM t WHERE … — removes specific rows DELETE FROM t — removes all rows (slow) TRUNCATE TABLE t — wipes all rows instantly, resets IDs
Perform calculations across many rows and return a single result.
💡 GROUP BY groups rows so functions run per group.

blocks.text:
SELECT
  s.name,
  g.score
FROM students AS s
INNER JOIN grades AS g
  ON s.id = g.student_id;

blocks.html: INNER JOIN returns only matching rows from both tables.
